scope: Constructed mechanistic diagnostic in a small equational list theory; not an established benchmark and not mathematical novelty.
claim_tested: Can a generic checked lemma enumerator reuse intermediate lemmas not supplied in its initial library, and does failure-guided ranking help beyond ordinary completion?
candidate_grammar: List variables X,Y,Z, nil, unary reverse, binary append; at most five AST nodes per term; pairs with equal finite-test signatures; canonical variable renaming; well-founded lexicographic path ordering.
counterexample_screen: All assignments of X,Y,Z to lists of length at most two on alphabet {0,1}; only a screen, never an acceptance certificate.
proof_acceptance: Separate structural-induction/rewrite checker; primitive definitions plus previously checked equations; no finite-model acceptance.
training: reverse(reverse(X))=X; record failed normal forms from its direct and induction attempts; no held-out equation used to construct or rank candidates.
baselines: cold generic completion per held-out theorem
human-designed normalization oracle (non-competing diagnostic upper bound)
held_out: Fixed compositional reverse/append equations, plus definition-only equations as a distribution-shift control. No within-test library updates in the retention comparisons.
accounting: Charge grammar construction, all finite evaluations, candidate construction/ranking, all search attempts including failures, and kernel checks. Report component counts and elapsed seconds separately. Proxy-operation budgets are not FLOP or hardware equivalence.
randomness: Deterministic execution; random-order candidate control uses fixed seeds 11, 23, 47.
success_threshold: No predeclared expected winner. Report failure-guided ranking advantage only if it beats retained generic completion at matched all-in budgets. A positive reuse-only result is proof-library learning, not evidence of a new mathematical or phenomenological principle.
limitations: Small trusted custom checker rather than Lean
Selection/design choices precede this run but are not independent external preregistration
